title: Polyoxometalate-based all-inorganic open frameworks
claim: Bridging a Preyssler {P5W30} cluster into an all-inorganic framework preserves reversible multi-electron redox and raises electronic conductivity relative to the discrete cluster, while the bridging metal and encapsulated cation tune the optical response.
explanation: Photodoping reduces the Co-bridged framework W12 by an average of about 10 electrons per cluster without loss of crystallinity, and the reduced phase conducts about three orders of magnitude better than the native crystal. Across Mn-, Fe-, Co-, Ni-, Cu-, and Zn-bridged analogues, diffuse-reflectance spectra keep the discrete {P5W30} profile plus linker d–d bands, Na+ inside the SBU can be replaced by other cations, and pellet conductivity is at least one order of magnitude higher than unbridged {P5W30}, which the review assigns to the bridging metals assisting charge transport.
scope: Preyssler-type {NaP5W30} all-inorganic frameworks bridged by divalent first-row transition metals, especially W12 and the W13 series.
conditions: W12 from K14NaP5W30O110 and CoCl2·6H2O at 90 °C in 1 M LiCl at pH 2; W13 by reflux of the potassium salt with metal chlorides at pH 1; photochemical reduction used to keep crystallinity.
caveats: Conductivity comparisons are for the reported crystals or pressed pellets. Hydrolytic stability and rigidity are stated for the delocalized-electron frameworks in these studies, not for all POW frameworks.
